notes:
Batch Q (venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, carbamazepine, betahistine, cinnarizine). All quotes checked FOUND on 2026-10-17 with the shared lib/text.mjs quoteFound (same normalisation as verify.mjs). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked).
REUSED SOURCES (defined in batch D, not redefined here): mhra-dsu-antidepressants-2026, mhra-dsu-ssri-pph, mhra-dsu-sjw-antiepileptics.
NO UK PRODUCT: desvenlafaxine (clinic 50 mg tablets): no emc result by ingredient or trade name, no MHRA Products SPC/PIL/licence (only incidental mentions in other products' leaflets). Marked no-uk-product with no rules.
FORMULATION GAPS: cinnarizine 25 mg (clinic product) is not licensed in the UK; UK SmPCs are for 15 mg tablets only (emc brand SmPC 371, last updated 2023, motion sickness only; two MHRA generic SPCs, which also cover vestibular disorders). Stated in the formulation note; doses are given in 15 mg tablets as the sources state. Venlafaxine: only the 75 mg prolonged-release capsule SmPC used (matches clinic product). Duloxetine: two UK generic 30 mg SmPCs (emc 12320, 13592), same 4.1/4.3/breastfeeding text; most quotes from 12320. Carbamazepine: Tegretol tablets SmPC (100/200/400 mg) only.
CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules): (1) Cinnarizine and porphyria: one UK SPC (Teva, 2021) lists porphyria in 4.3 (contraindicated); the brand SmPC and the Viatris 2026 SPC say use should be avoided (4.4). Two rules kept. (2) Duloxetine breastfeeding: SmPC not recommended vs SPS use with caution (SSRIs/TCAs preferred). (3) Venlafaxine breastfeeding: SmPC decide continue/discontinue vs SPS use with caution with infant monitoring (same level, kept as two rules). (4) Carbamazepine pregnancy: SmPC should not be used unless benefit outweighs risk (avoid) vs BUMPS can be used if recommended by a specialist when no safer option (caution). (5) Carbamazepine HLA-A*3101: SmPC "may be considered if benefits exceed risks" vs MHRA DSU "only after careful consideration of the benefits and risks" (same direction; both quoted).
INTERNAL SMPC INCONSISTENCY: Carbamazepine trigeminal neuralgia section says "doses of 1600mg ... may be needed" and also "Maximum recommended dose is 1200mg/day"; both stated in the dosing item.
BRAND PRESCRIBING: carbamazepine is MHRA antiepileptic category 1 (MHRA DSU Nov 2017; SPS monitoring and switching pages): maintain epilepsy patients on a specific manufacturer's product. SPS says switching is not usually an issue for non-epilepsy uses. No brand-prescribing statement found for the other medicines.
INTEGRATOR NOTES: (a) carbamazepine rules with other "prednisolone" and "dexamethasone" match by ingredient, so they will also fire for the ear/eye combination products that contain these steroids; add otherFormulations (systemic forms only) once batch AE writes those files. Ciprofloxacin rules (duloxetine contraindication, carbamazepine) already use otherFormulations to exclude the ciprofloxacin ear drops. (b) Venlafaxine and duloxetine have rules for group:serotonergic and also group:ssri / group:snri / group:tricyclic-antidepressant because the SmPCs name these classes; a pair such as venlafaxine + sertraline may therefore show two alerts. (c) Carbamazepine uses explicit fluconazole rather than group:azole-antifungal, so topical azoles are not flagged. (d) Group memberships: venlafaxine in qt-prolonging is from its own SmPC (postmarketing QTc/TdP cases; the SPS QT list does not name venlafaxine). Cinnarizine in sedating-antihistamine is from its SmPC ("As with other antihistamines" plus somnolence); the SPS antihistamines-in-breastfeeding page does not mention cinnarizine. Carbamazepine in cyp3a4-inducer and cyp3a4-strong-inducer from "potent inducer of CYP3A4".
NOT VERIFIABLE / LIMITS: the 4.8 frequency tables for venlafaxine, duloxetine, carbamazepine and cinnarizine (brand) are garbled in page text, so adverseCommon uses the SmPC summary sentences (very common/most common lists) rather than full tables. Elderly age rules use 65 years as the trigger where the SmPC says only "elderly" (venlafaxine, duloxetine); carbamazepine states 65 years. No SPS breastfeeding page found for carbamazepine, betahistine or cinnarizine; no BUMPS leaflet for betahistine or cinnarizine (404). Hormonal contraception with carbamazepine is set to caution ("alternative non-hormonal forms of contraception are recommended"), not avoid.
AUDIT (second check, 2026-10-17, see audit/P-Q.md): venlafaxine REMOVED from qt-prolonging. The SPS QT list does not name it, and its own SmPC 5.1 says a thorough QTc study showed no clinically relevant QT prolongation even at a supra-therapeutic 450 mg/day; post-marketing QTc/TdP reports were mainly in overdose or with other risk factors. This matches the policy used for mirtazapine (batch P). Venlafaxine's own avoid rule toward group:qt-prolonging is kept. Venlafaxine opioid rule narrowed to tramadol (the SmPC names specific serotonergic opioids; codeine is not among them). Duplicate venlafaxine insulin rule removed (group:antidiabetic already includes the insulins). Added venlafaxine uncontrolled-hypertension (caution: control BP before starting). Desvenlafaxine re-checked (emc search and MHRA products index): still no UK product. Cinnarizine 25 mg: MHRA products lists only 15 mg tablets and 20 mg/40 mg cinnarizine/dimenhydrinate combinations; the combination SmPC in the clinic map (emc 15869) is correctly not used.
